If the leave cost is negligible within one sortie on the MVP roster, that is a **finding recorded and not repaired** (Formulas, `cap_versus_leave`) — no pressure is invented to make capping matter. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(the Graph has since answered ASK-BS-G1(b), LSG:794: a welded section's stub leaks from the home network once the seam valve is opened, so capping does pay for the weld donor; on a derelict you leave, capping is still never the better trade at the MVP, which is why cap-or-leave is not a design-test row)* *Why.* A required cap would be a hidden gate (IA-26); an auto-cap on pickup would delete Pillar 1's consequence. *Pillar.* P1 (the hiss is truth), P5. *Decided.* run ruling R14.
199	
200	**BS-9 — Pick up and carry: never auto-carried; the carry-admitted set is closed.** *Rule.* A yield is picked up by a lit TAP (`pickup`, IA-28): a CARRIED-class def needs hands free (no carried instance; `BUSY` if one is held), moves LOOSE_WORLD to CARRIED, sets `carry_ref` through the Controller's `set_carry_ref` and the instance through Suit's `set_carried` (IA-28, SE-13). **Closing IA Open Question 17: a yield is never auto-carried**, confirming IA-25's locked text, so the lit-pickup cost and cap-before-carry sequencing stand. While carrying: gait is `V_CARRY`, no run (PC-8); stagger keeps the module and downed drops it (PC-8, PC-9); the **chest lamp stays available** (user decision 2026-10-26; PC-8's "beam off while carrying" is a Controller playtest lever, not reopened here); `throw_glowstick` and `equip_tool` are `BUSY` (IA-29, SE-11). **The admitted interactions while carrying are exactly four verbs: `drop` plus the three carry-admitted rows (`install_module` on a compatible HARDPOINT, `pod_hop` on the POD_CONSOLE, V4 `set_opening` on a door face), the same set Interaction counts as 'drop and the three carry-admitted rows' (IA-28, AC-IA-78, AC-IA-154) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: `drop` (IA-28); `install_module` on a HARDPOINT whose `compatible_defs(h)` lists the carried def (MSA-26, carve-out C1, verbatim: "while carrying, `interact` on a HARDPOINT subject whose `compatible_defs(h)` lists the carried instance's def is admitted, alongside `drop`"); `pod_hop` on the POD_CONSOLE (WM-8; PCI:694 "`carry_ref` is kept and the module travels with the pod (Boarding & Salvage's rule)"); and V4 `set_opening` on a door face (the row Interaction flags `admitted_while_carrying`, IA-28; a lit, in-reach, bare-hand QUIET TAP; `carry_ref` unchanged; a V6 vent hatch and every `begin_*` stay `BUSY`).** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* `toggle_beam` stays available as an actor verb. Every other world target stays prompt-less and `BUSY` (IA-5). The collision with IA-5, IA-28 and V-13 ("every `interact` mode except `drop` is `BUSY`") and PC-8 was real and is closed (C-BS-1, ASK-BS-I1 answered): Interaction adds the POD_CONSOLE `pod_hop` and HARDPOINT `install_module` rows with `admitted_while_carrying` true (registry: `admitted_while_carrying`; IA-2, IA-28, IA-40); `berth` and `unberth` are not carry-admitted (they sit on the DOCK_CONSOLE, which is BUSY while carrying; the `berth` verb is declared LOUD and `unberth` QUIET: one `U_LOUD` push at the berth apply, so berthing is a loud act the web hears; Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D59, with Interaction IA-40 changing `berth` from QUIET to LOUD) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the wording refreshes to PC-8, IA-5, IA-28 and V-13 stay with the Controller and Interaction (ASK-BS-C1). *Fallback, written as an edge case and not as a design, and **not shippable for the MVP**:* if the console row is refused, the module is dropped before the press and stays aboard; the carry-home branch is lost. That removes the loop the MVP exists to test (cut a module free, carry it home under rising Attention, install it), so the producer must treat a refusal of either row (the POD_CONSOLE or the HARDPOINT) as a **stop**, not a degrade: the same loss follows from a refused HARDPOINT row, which removes the carried install. *Why.* PCI:694 and WM:414 already grant the console press while carrying and MSA-26 carve-out C1 the seated install, so a refusal is a cross-GDD conflict and not a Boarding degrade; the collision was wording plus two missing rows, which Interaction has since added (ASK-BS-I1 answered, OQ-BS-5 closed; formerly a blocking dependency), so all four carry-admitted verbs have a declaration (the door row is Interaction's, IA-28, delegated ruling R21). *Pillar.* P5 (the haul home is the loop), P2 (the escape verb stays one press). *Decided.* run rulings R3, R7, R8.
201	
202	**BS-10 — Doors are the carry's terrain.** *Rule.* While carrying, the carrier may pass an OPEN door and may operate a CLOSED one with the door's ordinary lit V4 `set_opening` press (a bare-hand TAP of `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` 30 [PLACEHOLDER], QUIET, IA-24), with the module still in hand; the drop, open, lit pickup cycle is retired (IA-5, IA-28, PC-8). Doctrine: **open on the way in, carry through on the way out**; a door the player shut behind them (a legal Pillar 3 containment act) costs `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` on the way out (the figure D.1 already charges per `n_closed`, so no route figure changes). Content constraint (not a lint): no SYSTEM-origin door close on a carry route at MVP, because a surprise close on the carry route costs the carrier `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` they did not choose (ASK-BS-I2 stays as written); a closing door whose leaf overlaps a foot box retries each tick and lands on the first clear tick (IA-24). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Costs the doctrine used to leave out.** (1) *Preconditions.* The reference figures (D.1) assume `door_airlock_n` already OPEN (the player opened it on the way out) and `door_cargo_s` CLOSED at home, and both A doors CLOSED at the start; a door found otherwise changes `n_closed`, and AC-BS-6 fixes the starting state. (2) *The cooled spine.* Leaving `door_a_spine_machine` open on the way in mixes lethal cold into `a_spine` by `K_OPEN` conduction, and the carry back through it is the cost; it is Derelict Authoring's open-door projection (DA D.18), cited in D.4 and not recomputed. (3) *Discoverability:* the door's own plate is present while carrying (Visual/Audio step 11); X-BS-12 now observes that testers press it without dropping (AC-BS-124); the cold that the player perceives before the crossing is X-BS-13 (AC-BS-125); the first-door choice and the leading element that pulls toward `scr_a` are X-BS-14 (AC-BS-126, a sightline pass with Derelict Authoring). *Why.* Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R21 (user delegated all remaining calls): admit V4 `set_opening` while carrying, the creative-director lean already applied in Interaction IA-28 (G2): pressure should come from choices, not an unreadable lock-out; a TAP needs no free hands and the lamp is chest-mounted. *Pillar.* P3. *Decided.* run ruling R3 (level-designer LD-R4), amended by delegated ruling R21 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
203	
204	**BS-11 — Weight is the body, never a number.** *Rule.* Mass never changes `V_CARRY` or the carry noise (IDB-21, `NOISE_PER_TICK` carry 1 [PLACEHOLDER]); haul cost per tile is identical for a 90 kg cell and a 6 kg core (IDB F-13). The only weight surfaces are the Suit's body cue, `cue_load = max(carried_class, stowed_class)` (SE-28, breath with a load signature, tools excluded), and structure: one carried instance, hands full, and the HEAVY `part_hull_plate` with `stack_max` 1. A stowed HEAVY masks every carried class (SE-28, SE OQ-8; `STOWED_CUE_FLOOR_CLASS` [PLACEHOLDER] MEDIUM). **No pack capacity, encumbrance meter, pod scale or weight number is added** (SE-12 "no pack capacity and no weight limit"; IDB-21). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **A stowed HEAVY item disables run** (user ruling D18, option (a)): while any HEAVY item is stowed (the 30 kg `part_hull_plate` is the MVP case) the actor cannot run, so the plate is not a free second carry slot that undercuts the single-`carry_ref` bottleneck; no grams term is added and `V_CARRY` and `NOISE_PER_TICK` stay locked; the run rule is the Controller's (PC-8) and the roster the Item DB's. *Why.* A weight number is an inventory screen by another name (SE-12). *Pillar.* P1. *Decided.* run ruling R4.
205	
206	**BS-12 — The pod-hop cargo rule.** *Rule.* **What crosses with the pod is what the seated crew holds:** per seat one CARRIED instance (`carry_ref`, unchanged — instance-table row 12, IDB:450) plus the STOWED stacks (SE-12). **Pod capacity is the number of seats** (`seat_pod_1`, one at MVP, DA-3, WM-5; Boarding's structural rule); Web Map's `CAPACITY` reason is another system's runtime cap, unreachable at MVP (WM-9), and never a cargo or mass reason. **The bound on weight is structural** — one carried module, hands full, no run, every other verb `BUSY`, the HEAVY stack cap, the body cue — never a number, never a pod scale, never a refusal reason that reads module-body state (IA-11). No module rides unaccompanied; a module left in a dock room stays aboard as left (WM-28). `pod_hop` aborts any open channel (`ABORT(BODY)`) and a cut ledger older than `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] is gone on return (IA-40, IA-16). On arrival the actor is IDLE with `carry_ref` intact, then CARRY_WALK on the first non-NONE octant (PCI:694). The module rides in the arms through the pod leg; the carry burden does not: it is pushed only while the holder is aboard the non-home locus body where the salvage was taken, so it stops when the seat enters the pod and does not resume at home (EC-BS-63) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*. **One module per hop at MVP**, so a second useful module costs a second `HOP_FUEL_ML` [PLACEHOLDER] payment (WM-20). At Web Map's published figures that payment is 2 percent of the home tank, so fuel is a campaign clock shared with the reactor and not the cap on a haul (design-time, `modules_per_fuel`, Formulas; C-BS-14); the pressure on the haul is the hands, the walk and the tell. The routed thread "pod capacity and weight limit the haul" is thereby honoured structurally and not as a number, which **conflicts in letter** with SE-12 and IDB-21 and is flagged for creative-director review (C-BS-2, resolved for MVP by creative-director, 2026-10-26; revisit at the kill/continue playtest). Option B (a cargo cradle with a class-point ceiling) is the recorded Vertical Slice upgrade path with its asks pre-listed (Open Questions OQ-BS-1); any future cradle must be a visible physical surface the player loads by hand, and any refusal a world consequence (the pod visibly will not seal), never a text reason naming mass. *Why.* Zero new machinery, no oracle, and the concept loop is "find one salvageable system". *Pillar.* P1 (no readout), P3 (hands-full is the cost). *Decided.* run ruling R4; creative-director ruling D-CD-2.
207	
208	**BS-13 — Retreat and abandon are legal, free and deliberate.** *Rule.* The sortie's declared breach-retreat conditions (the ask at AT:380):
209	
210	| # | Condition | Effect | Owner rule |

content.thinking: Reading through all 1700 lines will take a while, but I'll continue in larger chunks. I'm noting some overlapping phrasing in BS-9 and BS-5 about the exact set of verbs and exceptions listed, trying to reconcile whether these restate the same facts consistently.

content.content:
210	| # | Condition | Effect | Owner rule |
211	|---|---|---|---|
212	| a | Leave the locus body by any route, normally the dock plus the pod console | the hop is **always allowed** during a TELL or BREACH (the escape verb) | WM-26 |
213	| b | Departure from a non-home locus body | ends a BREACH when the last recorded occupant leaves; a hop does not interrupt a TELL, but it voids the due-run breach (TELL to CALM, `ABORTED`, no STRESS, no beacon, rearm set) if every seat recorded in the locus body at tell entry has left it by then; a home-ship locus is not voidable, and 'the lights you left on' is the price (user ruling, D46) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | AT-22 |
214	| c | Stillness and darkness | a TELL aborts when `L < theta_HOLD` for `ABORT_HOLD_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER]; while salvage is held aboard the wreck the carry burden keeps `L` rising (the decay is suspended, Attention F-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*, so this condition is reached only after (d); escalation freezes while `L < theta_HOLD` (user ruling X4, behaviour-keyed; Attention's AT-9/AT-10) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | AT-10 |
215	| d | `drop` the carried module, anywhere | legal, free, exempt from the lit rule; the actor then runs at `V_RUN` 3 vs `V_CARRY` 1, unless a HEAVY item is stowed, in which case run is disabled and the retreat is at `V_WALK` 2 (user ruling D18) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | IA-28, IA-6, PC-8 |
216	| e | A downed actor | drops the module (the Controller clears `carry_ref`; Interaction's hook runs at divisor 1 after the Controller's, so the module is a loose item **within one tick**, IA-28) | PC-9, SE-13 |
217	
218	An abandoned module persists in `loose[]` as left and the derelict persists as left (WM-24, WM-28, IA-28); dropped in the dark it cannot be re-taken until something lights it (IA-28). **There is no forced drop, no hop refusal with cargo, and no tool kills a horror**: nothing is a weapon (anti-pillar), and the MVP kit has no repel tool (`tool_suppressant` is removed, user ruling X6 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the HE-39 repel stays a dormant [CUT-FIRST] interface). A horror met during a carry is answered by retreat, stillness, darkness or 'drop the cargo', which the user confirmed as the intended price of hauling (D63: Horror's figures have a carrier who keeps the cargo struck on 7 of 18 draws, with `R_SNAP_PX` 48 the lever); Horror places nothing in salvage and has no edge to author (HE:376, Designed). Every sortie step from the cut to the hop (steps 8 to 12) therefore has a legal exit. *Why.* A carried module that cannot be abandoned would turn a tell into a sentence. *Pillar.* P2, P3; anti-pillar (not a combat game). *Decided.* run rulings R13, R25. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Gating note (ruled; numbers pending).** The conditions are legal as written, and the decision they serve (keep walking, or set it down) is made live by the ruling of OQ-BS-27 (option B: the carry-state intake plus the lengthened carry, D.2 and D.3). It is live in kind (the tell opens inside the carry, holding cargo never outwaits it, and a drop does) and thin in margin: Attention's recalibration is run (F-26) and leaves a live share of 140 permille of the tell draw at 28 tiles, none at 21 to 24, and 66 to 140 permille over the lit pre-lift dwell sweep (D.2, D.3); the pass line is the boarding spike's (AC-BS-132, delegated ruling R5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*. **The stake of walking on** (named so that the choice is read and not learned as a clock) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: a walker whose drawn tell is shorter than the carry ahead arrives after `breach_due_T` and takes the breach (STRESS on the locus body, the beacon, the web's attention at the rim), a walker who arrives first voids it at no cost (AT-22), and the draw is never shown (P1); at the placeholders walking on wins in about 86 percent of draws at the reference carry, which Attention measures (AC-AT-134); OQ-AT-36 is decided (leave it, measured; delegated ruling R21, 2026-10-28) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. **Precondition (answered)** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R21; G1, the publisher's answer stands and Boarding conforms)*: a horror may path or stand in `a_spine` at the MVP (Horror E-HE-59, HE-26 and Horror's Dependencies row for Boarding & Salvage; ASK-BS-H1, OQ-BS-33 answered). No bypass and no wider spine is required or asked: the spine is the 3-wide corridor with no side step (DA-48, 3 x 23) and the legal-exit claim stands, because every step from the cut to the hop (steps 8 to 12) still has a legal exit and the exit is priced, not free. A carrier who meets a horror in the spine has the ruled answers and no new one: drop the cargo (BS-13 d) and walk back the way it came, which may be toward the cold `a_machine` (a priced exit, not a sentence); stand still and go dark if no other light reaches the seat (HE-13); or shut a door behind it (V4 `set_opening` on a door face is carry-admitted, BS-9, and a closed leaf is solid to the horror, HE-26). A carrier who keeps the cargo is struck on 7 of 18 draws with `R_SNAP_PX` 48 the lever (D63, confirmed as the price of hauling). The pressure of being met in the one corridor of the carry is the dread Pillars 2 and 3 aim for. A spine end that is a dead end failing Horror's `DEAD_END_NARROW` lint is Derelict Authoring's defect (E-HE-26), not a Boarding rule. No story is opened for BS-13's decision-bearing rows or for the tell acceptance rows that need a sortie-produced tell (AC-BS-72, AC-BS-122, AC-BS-123, the crossing clause of AC-BS-14b) until AC-BS-123 passes on the regenerated `REF_GOLDEN`. The fixture-armed mechanics rows (AC-BS-17, 18, 34, 35, 87, 93) test Attention's and Web Map's owned behaviour with `attention_arm_tell` and stay open as contract tests.
219	
220	**BS-14 — Field checks: the procedure and the ladder (class (d) hooks).** *Rule.* Interaction owns the `field_check` channel (IA-30); Sanity owns lure data, `lures[]`, the ledger and `record_falsification(player_id, check_kind, subject_ref, outcome)` (SN-17, Class B); the Item DB owns true mass and the junk defs (IDB-22, VS-A). **Boarding owns the procedure**: when a crew runs the ladder during a sortie, its preconditions, and what each rung costs in the sortie's budget. The ladder is SN-21's, cheapest first:
221	
222	| Rung | Instrument | Cost inside the sortie | Tier | Precondition |
223	|---|---|---|---|---|
224	| 1 | The **weight breath-step**: pick it up and feel `cue_load` (SE-28) | the pickup, then `drop` if suspect; no tool, no channel | MVP on real modules and the hull plate; lures VS-A | the stowed class is below the carried class under test (`STOWED_CUE_FLOOR_CLASS` [PLACEHOLDER]): **drop the plate first** |
225	| 2 | **SCAN** (`check_kind` SCAN) | `FIELD_CHECK_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER], lit, scanner in hand (slot 3), plus the swap | MVP (the scanner is an honest anchor, SN-19) | scanner held; hands free |
226	| 3 | **PALETTE** (the violet or flesh leak on the sprite) | sight only | VS-A | the Perception Filter (Designed) |
227	| 4 | The **authored-absence read**: undisturbed dust, a missing verdict trail, a dried trail on a module's own fitting (DA:1189; FT:71 "a candidate field check, never a guarantee") | walking and looking | MVP | exists only where Derelict Authoring placed a dead fault |
228	| 5 | **The trip home** | the dearest | MVP | none |

230	A rung can fail to *apply* (a stowed HEAVY, no scanner, no authored trail) but never lies in the MVP; no result is stored as truth about a lie in `interaction.state` (IA-30). The design test is Sanity's `C_check <= 0.05 x T_home` (SN-21 and the class (d) design test of SN D.7, where `T_home` is "the one-way trip home with the item"), and the break-even walk-versus-scan distance `d*` is 5 tiles (SN-18, AC-SN-70); whether SCAN passes the test on the MVP routes is a finding in Formulas (`check_cost_ratio`), not a rule. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **SCAN is an explicit MVP exception to SN-21 and SN D.7's 5 percent test**: it passes on no MVP route (0.250 to 0.056), class (d) ships no junk for it to disprove, and the exception lapses at VS-A, where either the junk placement keeps `T_home` at least 3120 ticks (D.7) or `FIELD_CHECK_TICKS` is bounded at 66 or less (`C_check` = 36 + 66 = 102 and `20 * 102` = 2040 is at most the 2055 ticks of reading (c) for `htr_a`; it still fails readings (a) and (b)). IA-30 reserves `check_kind` HEFT (the lift-and-weigh) and PALETTE for VS-A; at MVP rung 1 is perception only (SE-28) and records nothing, and the recorded form is HEFT at VS-A. **"Drop the plate first" is not yet performable**: the plate is a STOWED stack, `drop` (IA-28) releases only the carried instance, and no in-world way to shed a stowed stack is written (ASK-BS-S1); until one is, the ladder skips rung 1 and uses SCAN or the trip home. MVP exercises: the breath-step on real carried modules and the plate, SCAN, and the absence read on `scr_a` (BS-17). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **No scanner additions at the MVP** (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D66): no scanner cooldown, no within-band magnitude-only GLIDE and no rebuild of Sanity's D.12; Sanity's rung-mix telemetry (AC-SN-165) decides later. Class (d) itself is VS-A; its acceptance rows are **deferred**, blockers "junk defs (IDB-22) + the Perception Filter + SN-21", and the blind two-clip audio identification test of the load cue (SE RK-2, at least 90 %) is a precondition of the VS-A breath-step. *Why.* The trip home is the fallback, not the only reveal (Pillar 4(d)). *Pillar.* P4. *Decided.* run ruling R17.
231	
232	**BS-15 — The lie is in the prize, never in the price.** *Rule.* A hallucination may lie about **what** a module is or **whether** it is worth taking. It may never lie about **what taking it costs**: the cut's noise, the stub's hiss, the load's breath, the carry's pace, the time, the air. Each price channel is truthful by its owner's rule: noise is Attention's (IA-33, ART 2.7), hiss and room air are on the Graph's closed consequence list (LSG:44), the breath comes from true `mass_g` (SE-28, IDB-22), the pace is `V_CARRY` (PC-8), the beam is the truth anchor (EM). The carry burden is a price as well, and in the fiction it is keyed on place: **the web hears the taking at the wreck**, so the burden runs while salvage is held aboard the locus it was taken from and stops at the pod (EC-BS-63); no hallucination changes it (Attention owns it, F-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*. A phantom has no subject and answers like an unlit object (EM-21, IA-13), so reaching for one is not a free oracle. The MVP ships class (b) only. *Why.* If the price could lie the bargain is meaningless and the player stops making it; if only the prize can lie, every take is a bet on one's own perception and the ladder is how it is bought down. *Pillar.* P4, P1. *Decided.* creative-director guard rail G-11.
233	
234	**BS-16 — The faucet is finite and persists as left.** *Rule.* Salvage is the only faucet (IDB-29): the authored module-node list (A 18 module nodes, B 22, home 26, DA-21), the seeded loose ledger (9 placements, DA-26) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* and `salvage_yield` (deterministic, no RNG, salvage-once, IDB-17). A SALVAGED slot is a tombstone and stays so (LSG:243). A left derelict stands exactly as left (WM-24, WM-28). The remaining salvage in a room is read from the room (the empty pedestal rect, LY-20; the scorched kerf; hissing or capped stubs; an empty shelf), never from a count (ART 7.4). Repeated as Derelict Authoring asks (DA:1239): **the faucet is the authored node list and loose placements; the ledger is finite; and a cheap field read exists for a failed module** (BS-14, BS-17). Sortie-level loose-item rules only: an abandoned item persists (BS-13); a yield appears at the node anchor; items are section-local, so a weld or detach moves nothing (LY-22). Compartment-level "first entry" knowledge is **not** Boarding's and is declined at MVP: Web Map keeps the derelict level (`FIRST_BOARDED`, WM-28), Layout keeps only `room_at`, and the owner is the Vertical Slice Knowledge Codex's PROFILE-scoped data (answering LY Open Question 12). *Why.* A faucet the player can read from the room and cannot refill is what makes scarcity push inward; a count, a first-entry flag or any regrowth would each be a meter or a farm. *Pillar.* P5 (a finite persisting list vs a refillable crate, finite). *Decided.* run rulings R11, R20.
235	
236	**BS-17 — The taught payoff of sortie A is `htr_a`; `scr_a` is optional restraint.** *Rule.* The **reference first sortie** cuts `htr_a` (MEDIUM 12000 g, power-only so no stub, in `a_machine`) and installs it in the vacant `hp_cargo_heater`, which arms PWR-OVL at home (MSA:28, DA-12, DA:855): a consequence the player caused. **`a_machine` is the one lethal-cold room**, so the reference sortie is a *hazard* sortie: the carried round trip through an unbreathable stretch and the hazard crossing are bounded by Derelict Authoring's lints (BS-20) and the room's tell is the frost creeping over the sill of the closed door before it is opened. The dead scrubber `scr_a` (FAILED, `hp` 2000, HEAVY 40000 g, `a_life`) is a legal cut whose carry home **now has a destination** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (user ruling D72: a vacant scrubber hardpoint at home, with two or three competing hardpoints, which are Assembly's data and Derelict Authoring's placement; there is still no `remove_module`, MSA-28), so installing it installs a FAILED module with no take-back (BS-18) and the beat is a stake and not only "the time the loot was garbage" (concept Key Dynamics); it remains Derelict Authoring's *quiet alternative* (cut it and leave; DA:1157). This GDD does **not** script `scr_a` as the first or the reference cut (IDB-14): the first cut is `htr_a`, and reading `scr_a` is what its destination is for. *Falsifier of record for `scr_a` before the cut* (DA OQ-V10): **only what is on the Graph's closed consequence list** — lamp brightness (its NODE_LANTERN dark, the lamp-free neighbour branch, DA-24, DA:1445), the room's own O2 and temperature as the body feels them, draught — plus **SCAN as the priced second instrument**. The cut's missing hum is true-state audio in the consequence channel (LSG:976) but is not in LSG:44's enumerated list; Boarding uses it as true-state corroboration and does not make it the falsifier of record until the Graph rules (C-BS-4). On A's dead bus nothing hums, so the hum, like the lantern, falsifies 'running' only; the dead-bus analysis is unchanged; undisturbed dust is supporting verdict grammar (ART 6.5). **Weight cannot discriminate**: `scr_a` has the same def mass, 40000 g, as a healthy scrubber. **On a dead bus the closed-list witnesses falsify "running" only**: on A's dead bus no machine runs, so every lantern is dark, `scr_a`'s and `pump_a`'s alike (DA-24), and the room's O2 and temperature cannot tell an unpowered healthy scrubber from a FAILED one; health is discriminated by SCAN, or by waking the bus with the spare breaker (DA-25, AC-DA-111), after which `pump_a`'s lantern lights and `scr_a`'s stays dark. *Conditions (creative-director D-CD-3):* the beat is honest only if the falsifier works in playtest (playtest target X-BS-3, Game Feel and AC-BS-71); if it does not, the beat is a trap and the response is routed to the falsifier (the witnesses of record, the SCAN cost), because the content route is already committed (user ruling D72) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Conflicts routed: C-BS-3 (LS-26 "first V8" names `scr_a`), C-BS-4, C-BS-6 (DA playtest target X-DA-8). *Pillar.* P1 (no payoff-less carry is taught), P4, P5. *Decided.* run rulings R10, R18; creative-director D-CD-3.
237	
238	**BS-18 — Install at home: the precondition repeated.** *Rule.* `install_module {hardpoint_ref}` is Assembly's PLAYER TAP and its prompt exists iff the seat carries an instance whose def is in `compatible_defs(h)` for the focused HARDPOINT (immediate, never an oracle); the chain is M5 `install_module`, `release_carried`, `clear_carry_ref`, `sync_section` (MSA-26, MSA-27). `condition_bp` carries through, so installing a FAILED-hp instance installs a FAILED module (IDB-17, IDB-18). There is **no `remove_module`** in the MVP: V8 salvage is the only way a module leaves INSTALLED, so the choice at the hardpoint is final (MSA-28). The Item DB's `T_cycle` — **cut + carry + `cap_port` on the stubs + install** (Interaction's and Assembly's verbs) — is the cost of one salvage-then-reinstall (IDB F-15); repeated as Assembly asks (MSA T12): the install precondition is *carried, compatible per `compatible_defs(h)`, at a hardpoint*. The patch cap and decay clock persist through salvage and reinstall (IDB-18, provisional on a Graph ruling, IDB OQ-10). The welder and section cut cannot run while carrying (MSA-26). *Why.* The install is the one place where the haul becomes the ship, and a seat with no take-back is what makes the take at the derelict a commitment; repeating the precondition keeps the sortie's last step from being read as inventory management. *Pillar.* P5; anti-pillar (not a freeform builder). *Decided.* run ruling R3.
239	
240	**BS-19 — A dark dock must never be fatal: the hop-availability invariant (ruled 2026-10-27: the pod's status glow).** *Rule.* **No sortie state exists in which the hop is unavailable for want of light alone.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Mechanism (user ruling, OQ-BS-4 part (a), X2, D58, D70a):** the docked pod's dock-room prop carries a small **self-powered status glow** that counts as an **ordinary lit fixture** and not as a fourth `act_gate` exception: the POD_CONSOLE stands inside the glow's light shape, so `lit(POD_CONSOLE)` holds at every docked pod whatever the beam cell or the stick count, and `pod_hop` cannot answer `NOT_LIT` while the glow stands. The glow guarantees `lit(POD_CONSOLE)` at every docked pod; the DOCK_CONSOLE at the home airlock keeps its own lit gate and is not part of this invariant (IA-6, IA-40) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Interaction's refusal of a `pod_hop` lit exemption (IA-6, Open Question 31) **stands**; BS-5's lit-only rule has no exemption for the console. The glow belongs to the pod and not to the derelict bus, so it needs neither the player's cell nor a lit pickup nor a woken bus. **Ownership is joint:** Emitter State and Web Map guarantee the glow (LANDED: Emitter EM-3 (self-powered fixture class, subkind DOCK_STATUS) and EM-11, mutator E10 `set_dock_status` (called by Web Map in the `pod_at` apply) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; Web Map reverses its ASK-BS-W2 answer and accepts ASK-BS-W3), Derelict Authoring places it in every dock room and lints the placement, including that the console lies inside the glow's light shape, as a build error, and the art-director separates its luminance from the visible-unknown lamp (DA-27) and keeps it steady and un-modulated; Boarding states the invariant and its acceptance (AC-BS-51b, AC-BS-92). The glow is ON while the pod is docked and SYSTEM-switched (the player cannot switch it; Emitter State EM-3/EM-11), with its light footprint limited to the console cell *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, so it is an `I_light` term of every aboard row of D.2 (its output is `DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM` 500, `DOCK_STATUS_REACH_PX` 48 [PLACEHOLDER: Emitter], section emission at most 24 (Emitter C3) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; Attention must count it in its unswitchable set and recheck the abort floor, a note for Attention).
241	
242	*Cell policy (OQ-BS-4 part (b), X5, D70b, user ruling):* V7 `top_up` joins the MVP verb list (the Graph's LS-26 amendment) as a deliberate bare-hand TAP; `TOPUP_MODE` is VERB and `CELL_ENABLED` is on, so the lamp cell exists, is finite, and is refillable at a lit BATTERY port at home (Suit D.9: a credit never exceeds the deficit), and the Pillar 3 'go dark' lever exists. A spent cell therefore costs the sortie its light and not the way home. *What remains true.* A module dropped far from the dock in the dark still needs light to be re-taken (`pickup` is lit-only, BS-5; EC-BS-30), so with the cell spent and no sticks it is lost to that sortie: a cost and not a soft-lock, because the player walks to the lit console and hops. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
243	
244	*History, kept so the acceptance rows read.* Before the ruling, a player with the cell spent, zero sticks and an unlit console was in a true soft-lock and it was the expected end of a long lit session (D.10: about 4 survey sorties spend the cell), with the dock survivable (`a_dock` `T0` -6000 mC) so that no death and no restore ever fired; Interaction had refused the lit exemption, Web Map had declined the stronger lint, and the loose-glowstick fallback was unsound (a loose stick is unlit until thrown and `pickup` is lit-only). The existing mitigations (the two-stick `a_dock` shelf, `ls_a_dock_shelf`; the four-stick home airlock supply, `ls_air_locker`, DA-26; drop, throw, re-take, IA-29) still narrow the dark-drop case and are no longer load-bearing for the hop. **The invariant is BLOCKING for the implementation of this system** (stage-12 ruling after the CD-GDD-ALIGN concern: P5 says failure costs ship and body and never a soft-lock): the sortie is not implementation-complete, and the slice does not ship, while AC-BS-92 (a bounded reachability test over the matrix and the campaign-length strand cell) or AC-BS-51b (the placement lint and the console-in-glow check) is red; no sign-off replaces them. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
245	
246	*Mechanisms considered (history of the ruling).* **M1**, a console-only lit exemption in IA-6, was refused by Interaction and is not taken. **M3**, a reserved lamp charge only the console press can spend, was not taken. **M2**, a pod-owned console lamp, is the nearest: the ruled mechanism is a self-powered status glow on the docked pod's prop, an ordinary fixture and not a lamp off the derelict bus. Rejected throughout: allowing `throw_glowstick` while carrying (it removes the BS-5 cost of lighting the drop zone first). *Pillar.* P5, P2. *Decided.* run ruling R3 (level-designer LD-R6); the stage-12 CD-GDD-ALIGN revision made the invariant binding; the user ruled the mechanism and the cell policy on 2026-10-27 (OQ-BS-4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
247	
248	**BS-20 — Content-side sortie constraints are citations; one design target.** *Rule.* These Derelict Authoring bounds are lint-backed facts Boarding relies on and re-checks across **all five loaded sets** S0 to S4 and both sortie orders (never only the first sortie): a carried round trip to the farthest salvage through an unbreathable stretch inside Suit's vacuum budget `VACUUM_BUDGET_S` 27 s (22 tiles each way walking out and carrying back, 34 carried both ways; AC-SE-75a); A has no unbreathable stretch, so it binds B only *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, Suit R6 pod derivation)*; a hazard crossing of at most 7 tiles of lethal cold (5.6 s); `ESCAPE_ROUTE_BUDGET_PX` 1800, 600 when carrying (the endogenous-fault escape bound, DA-29, a different question from the module-saving bound); 18 / 22 module nodes (A / B); four loose parts *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the loose ledger (DA-28, DA-29, DA-21, DA-25, DA-26, DA-32). **Design target, not a lint and not registered:** a first sortie to A completes cut and carry-home in about five minutes of *player time* (concept Core Loop; measured as W_LOOP, home console press to install, with its median W_ABOARD part kept below Sanity's stage-1 point, D.1 and D.8; a long sortie that enters stage 1 is intended: Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D73 part (c) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* with `RESERVE_S` [PLACEHOLDER] and `CELL_S` [PLACEHOLDER] sufficient. The route itself is a minute-scale lower bound; the five minutes are listening, lighting, deciding and door choices, so nobody tunes the route up to hit five minutes by distance (`V_CARRY` is locked). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **One target:** W_LOOP (home console press to install) is the single five-minute target and every other figure derives from it: the design-expectation W_ABOARD is W_LOOP less the non-interactive pod legs and the home leg, about 259 s at the defaults, of which the lint guarantees about 229 s (Tuning Knobs, Design targets; OQ-BS-28 (d)) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, and the 300 s figure of D.8 and the 5-minute top of the X-BS-1 band are the stage-1 ceiling on the median, not second targets. The ruled decision carry of about 21 to 28 tiles (X3) lies with at most 7 tiles (336 px) of it inside `a_machine` (the lethal-cold cap, DA-28; DA-48 measures the carry from the cut point and its proposal puts 228 px there) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; whether a 1008 to 1344 px carried leg passes `ESCAPE_ROUTE_BUDGET_PX` 600 when carrying (DA-29, a different question from the module-saving bound) is Derelict Authoring's lint question (OQ-BS-31). This GDD's reading: the 600 px bound is the endogenous-fault escape bound and does not apply to a non-fault decision carry; Derelict Authoring states that it does not (DA-29, DA-48, AC-DA-161): no exemption is granted or needed, and a lint that rejects the ruled route fails AC-BS-52 (ASK-BS-D4 (e)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Sanity's dwell cost is cited and not set: `ABOARD_EXPOSURE` [PLACEHOLDER] (SN). **Subject budget:** Boarding adds no subject beyond the drops `P <= PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE` and forbids any rule here that seeds more loose items; the post-weld sortie S4 `{home+B, A}` already exceeds `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` by 24 (144 vs 120, DA OQ-DA-20, owned by Derelict Authoring and Interaction, C-BS-7). Node anchors are not published by Derelict Authoring, so every route figure in this GDD is marked as assumed and deferred to Layout's `route_length_px` (ASK-BS-D1). *Why.* The authored bounds are what keep a carried return survivable and a retreat legal across every loaded set; citing them and minting no lint of Boarding's own keeps Derelict Authoring the one owner of the geometry, while the design target names only the felt length. *Pillar.* P2, P5. *Decided.* run rulings R23, R24, R29.
249	
250	**BS-21 — Autosave after a cut.** *Rule.* "Section extraction" in SL-4 is **Assembly's detach** (BDY:341) and is already served by MSA-33's derived read `last_shape_change_T()`, polled by Save/Load; Boarding neither owns nor names it. For a **module** cut, a completed V8 should also shorten the loss window, following the same pattern: Interaction publishes a pure derived read of the last salvage-completion tick (the read `last_salvage_T()` (registry: `last_salvage_T`); **Boarding mints no name**, which is this GDD's answer to Save/Load OQ-24), Save/Load polls it under SL-5's gate and `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS`, and `DEATH_LOOP_WINDOW_TICKS` guards a doomed save (SL-4, SL-5, SL-7, SL-8). A tell defers through SL-5 soft row (b) (provisional; an absent Attention view counts as open and logs `GATE_INPUT_ABSENT`); a channel, stagger or transit defers through `GATE_SOFT_STATES`; DOWNED and DEAD are hard. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **User rulings X7, D14, D42, D17:** (a) any bound seat whose `vitals_state` is CRITICAL or worse is a third soft-gate input (a due save is deferred up to the cap, then written `RISKY`, with no glyph), also applied to `quit_risky`; (b) the fairness step-back: a death restore also steps back one generation when `T_downed - g_r.T` is under `W_MIN_WARNING_S x TICK_RATE` (600 ticks); (c) a post-DOWNED refractory of `W_MIN_WARNING_S x TICK_RATE` ticks. The module-cut event autosave, with the weld and seam-cut events, is **confirmed** (D17; the escape hatch is a data change and metric M5). Assembly's seam-cut event autosave is withheld while the self-inflicted RAGGED decompression runs (until the keep-side cut room has vented and its ports are capped or past the port ceiling, D54, MSA-33) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* and does not apply to a module cut, whose SEVERED descriptors are EXOGENOUS and open no row (a) window; the fault loss window (mean about 5400, max 10,800, ceiling 18,000 ticks, D55) is Assembly's and Save/Load's. The ruled text is Save/Load's (SL-5, SL-8); D.9 prints the gate list. `CARRY_WALK` is not a gate state, so an autosave may land mid-carry; a cut's SEVERED descriptors are EXOGENOUS and open no row (a) window. The read therefore cannot trap the player in a doomed state. The brief's push-event idea is not adopted (Boarding cannot emit one, BS-1). *Why.* The loss ceiling (340 s, 5.7 minutes: SL's `loss_max` of 20,400 ticks, D.9) is longer than a whole five-minute sortie *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *Pillar.* P5 (loss is not total). *Decided.* run ruling R6; ASK-BS-I4, ASK-BS-L1.
251	
252	**BS-22 — Art direction owned here: severed stubs, the cap piece, and one shared carried-module sprite.** *Rule.* Boarding owns the **art direction and states** of the severed-stub pieces (kit gap K-9; DA:526, DA:1341, DA:1465) for `/asset-spec`: one STUB per open fluid port; hissing until capped (the sound is Audio's); a cap piece after `begin_cap`; the pedestal rect stays (LY-20) and the scorched kerf is Interaction's V8 completion row; all **hue-less, matte, mechanical, no glow, no body vocabulary in any sprite, palette or sound brief** (ART 4.4; the flesh and violet palette is reserved for sanity leaks). All carried modules, real or (VS-A) phantom, draw as **one plain shape drawn once on the tool layer** (ART:512, ART:815), so a real and a phantom carry look alike; identity is known from the loose sprite at pickup and from the body cue, not from the carried sprite (closes IA Open Question 23). The carry frames keep the chest point and the forward beam arc unobstructed (ART:1221); pose is **ruled by the art-director: the module is held overhead**, centred over the helmet with its bottom edge at least 2 px above the crown, the sprite capped at 24 x 14 px so figure plus module is at most 71 px, under the 72 px wall front face (ART 8.2; AD-BS-1, AD-BS-2; C-BS-5 closed). The PC-8 phrase "below the lamp" is refreshed (refresh row 19). *Why.* A hue-less, matte stub stays on the truth side of the sane palette, and one shared carried sprite means a real and a phantom carry can be told apart only by the body cue and the checks, never by the drawing. *Pillar.* P1, P4 (parity). *Decided.* run rulings R21, R22.
253	
254	**BS-23 — Loose items and the sortie: what Boarding repeats.** *Rule.* Placement data is Derelict Authoring's ledger (DA-26), slots are Layout's (LY-22), the mechanism and holder are Interaction's (IA-28); Boarding adds only the sortie-level rules stated in BS-13 (abandon persists), BS-5 (dark drop needs light), BS-16 (the haul is finite). A module dropped then left on a section that is later welded or cut off moves with the section (items are section-local, LY-22). Wording refreshes owed to neighbours that say otherwise are listed in Cross-References and never edited here. *Why.* Restating loose-item ownership here would give one fact two writers; naming only the sortie-level consequences (abandon persists, a dark drop needs light, the haul is finite) keeps one owner per fact. *Pillar.* P5. *Decided.* run ruling R20.
255	
256	**BS-24 — What Boarding refuses (the anti-pillar rule).** *Rule.* The following do not exist in the sortie, and a rule anywhere in this GDD that implies one is a defect:
257	
258	| Refusal | Guard | Pillar or anti-pillar |
259	|---|---|---|
260	| Combat: no weapon on any def, no damage verb, no kill; the cutter cuts machines, never creatures | G-1 | not a combat game |
261	| Progression: nothing levels, unlocks or scores from salvage; the only progression is the ship's body and what the player learns (the knowledge persistence the failure contract depends on is not a progression this guard forbids) | G-2 | P5 / not a combat game |
262	| Construction: modules are pre-shaped; a take is an extraction and not a relocation; no `remove_module` | G-3 | not a freeform builder |
263	| Economy: no shop, currency, recipe, vendor, refill, loot table, rarity; salvage-once | G-4 | P5 |
264	| Readouts: no inventory screen, pack capacity, encumbrance meter, weight, value, condition or capacity number, pod scale | G-5 | P1 |
265	| Timers and meters: no sortie timer, no Attention meter (visual or audio), no `listen` verb | G-6 | P3 |
266	| Forced script: sortie order is a recommendation (DA-2); no forced drop, cap, required module or quest item; no payoff-less carry taught as the reference cut | G-7 | no authored story; P1 |
267	| PvP: no stealing from a crewmate's hands and no reward for harm (VS-B); the carry cost is the crew's shared cost; the only harm to a crewmate is the system-gated friendly-harm act, admitted only while the attacker's sanity is system-verified below the harm threshold (Sanity; IA-31), with a victim-visible tell and attribution to the web, so a sane player has no attack (P4(c)) | G-8 | no intentional PvP; P4(c) |
268	| Body metaphor in the senses: graft, severed, bleed are design prose only | G-9 | P1 sane palette |
269	| A win state in a haul: no "complete the ship", no collection checklist | G-10 | no win state |
270	| A price that lies (BS-15) | G-11 | P4 |
271	
272	Restraint and retreat are legal strategies with stated costs (BS-13). *Pillar.* the anti-pillars. *Decided.* run ruling R31; creative-director guard rails G-1 to G-11.

274	### States and Transitions
275	
276	**Boarding & Salvage has no stored state** (BS-1). The template requires a state table, so the table below is a **fixture and design vocabulary**: each label is a predicate over fields the owners already hold, computed and never written, never registered, never persisted, and never a name in any file, command or event. It exists so that the headless reference sortie (Acceptance Criteria) and the Game Feel arc can name "where in the sortie" without minting state. *(orchestrator ruling: the stage ruling R12 says "no Boarding state names"; the task requires this table; the resolution is to keep the table as test-fixture vocabulary, state this once, and let the labels be dropped or renamed at the checkpoint without touching any rule. Logged as a question.)*
277	
278	**The four owner axes the labels read** (nothing else is consulted):
279	
280	| Axis | Owner field | Values used |
281	|---|---|---|
282	| Where | `body_of_actor` / `actor_section` (BDY); `transit_state` (WM) | home body; derelict locus body; in transit (`IDLE`, `LEG`, `ARRIVING`, `BERTHING`) |
283	| What the hands do | `controller.state.loco_state` (PC) and `channel_ref` | `IDLE`, `WALK`, `RUN`, `CARRY_WALK`, `CHANNELLING`, `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED`, `IN_POD` |
284	| What is held | `controller.state.carry_ref` (PC-8), cross-checked with `suit.state.carried_id` (SE-13) | none / one carried instance |
285	| What the web is doing | Attention `phase` (AT) | `CALM`, `TELL`, `BREACH`, `SUBSIDING` |
286	
287	**Labels (derived, never stored):**
288	
289	| Label | Derived from | Entry | Exit | Legal transitions | Who may cause them |
290	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
291	| HOME | actor in the home body; `transit_state` `IDLE` | boot, or arrival from a hop | `pod_hop` Applied | to TRANSIT_OUT | the player (`pod_hop`, WM-8) |
292	| TRANSIT_OUT | `transit_state` `LEG` with origin home; `loco_state` `IN_POD` | `pod_hop` Applied (a body transfer; aborts any channel, IA-40) | `pod_arrive` / `pod_settle` after `HOP_LEG_TICKS` and `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` | to ABOARD_QUIET | Web Map's machine (WM-14); the player only by pressing the console |
293	| ABOARD_QUIET | actor in a derelict locus body; no `channel_ref`; hands free or a tool in hand; `phase` not `TELL`/`BREACH` | arrival; a channel ends or aborts; `drop` | a channel begins; `pickup`; a TELL opens | to ABOARD_JOB, LOADED, ABOARD_TELL | the player (verbs); Attention (phase) |
294	| ABOARD_JOB | `loco_state` `CHANNELLING` on `begin_cut`, `begin_cap` or `field_check` | channel `Applied` (lit, in reach) | completion; abort (IA-15: MOVED, CANCELLED, UNLIT, OUT_OF_REACH, TARGET_GONE, BODY, NOT_ELIGIBLE, RESTORE); a TELL opens (the channel is not aborted by it) | to ABOARD_QUIET, ABOARD_TELL | the player; the abort set; Attention (phase) |
295	| LOADED | `carry_ref` set; `loco_state` `CARRY_WALK` or `IDLE` | `pickup` Applied (IA-28) | `drop`; downed (PC-9); `install_module`; `pod_hop` carries it across (state persists) | to ABOARD_QUIET (drop), HOME (via hop), INSTALLED | the player; Suit's limiter via PC-9 (downed) |
296	| ABOARD_TELL | `phase` `TELL` and the actor in the locus body | Attention enters TELL (AT-8) | abort by stillness (AT-10), breach due, or departure | to ABOARD_QUIET (abort), ABOARD_BREACH, TRANSIT_BACK | Attention only; the player's restraint or departure shapes it |
297	| ABOARD_BREACH | `phase` `BREACH` or `SUBSIDING`, actor in `locus_body` (AT-15) | tell expiry | the last recorded occupant leaves a non-home locus body (AT-22) | to TRANSIT_BACK | Attention (the harm), the player (departure) |
298	| TRANSIT_BACK | `transit_state` `LEG` with origin a derelict; `loco_state` `IN_POD` | `pod_hop` Applied from a dock room (always allowed, WM-26) | arrival at home | to HOME (and still LOADED if `carry_ref` is set) | the player; Web Map's machine |
299	| INSTALLED | M5 `install_module` Applied (MSA-26) | the module seated in a hardpoint | **terminal for that module** (no `remove_module`, MSA-28; V8 salvage is the only way out) | none | the player (`install_module`) |
300	| DOWNED | `loco_state` `DOWNED` (Suit limiter FAILED, SE-24) | the limiter reaches FAILED | revive (VS-B); the solo give-up-and-reload action (user ruling D7 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*); `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` elapses, then DEAD, then restore from the newest autosave (SL-7) | to ABOARD_QUIET (revive), restore | Suit/Controller (the limiter); the host (restore) |
301	
302	**Transition rules worth stating once.**
303	
304	1. **LOADED is an overlay, not a place.** It combines with every aboard label (a tell during a carry is ABOARD_TELL and LOADED at once); the fixture reports both.
305	2. **Any aboard label may go to TRANSIT_BACK from any dock room with the pod docked there, whatever the cargo** (WM-26, WM:414 envelope). If the console row is refused (C-BS-1), a LOADED actor must first `drop` and the module stays aboard (Edge Cases).
306	3. **A tell does not interrupt a hop, and a hop does not interrupt a tell** (AT-22, WM-26), but a hop that leaves a derelict locus voids the due-run breach if every seat recorded at tell entry has left by then (AT-22; user ruling D46 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*); a departed derelict goes dormant and its state stands still (WM-24, LS-17).
307	4. **Restore returns each axis to its owner's snapshot** and the labels are recomputed: `CHANNELLING` and `STAGGERED` go to `IDLE`, `carry_ref` is restored with the Suit's instance and cross-checked (PC-17, SE-13 `SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH`); Interaction's `post_restore` never touches `carry_ref` (IA-28); a cut that completed before the autosave stands, one that did not is as if never begun (the ledger is Interaction's).
308	5. **Nothing here is guarded by Boarding.** Every transition is caused by a verb, a hop or an Attention phase that an owner validates; Boarding adds no guard, no timeout and no side effect to any of them.
309	
310	*Why.* A named, registered sortie machine would restate `loco_state`, the Attention phase and `transit_state` (run ruling R12). *Pillar.* P3 (the cost is in the steps, not in a state). *Decided.* run ruling R12 (the table kept as fixture vocabulary).
311	
312	### Interactions with Other Systems
313

364	**Scope and conventions (read first; every formula below uses them).** Every formula here is **design-time: not hashed, not persisted and never read by the simulation** (Boarding registers no state and no constant, BS-1, R1; the SN:529 precedent). Each is an analysis that the designers and the headless reference sortie can recompute, and each leans on an owner's formula **by name and never restates it**: `attention_integrator` (Attention), `held_mass_cue` (Suit), IDB F-13 `haul_cost` and F-15 `patch_launder` (`T_cycle`), SN D.7 (check cost), DA D.10 `cold_room_exposure`, WM D.4 `hop_fuel`, SL `loss_ticks`. Arithmetic is integer: `ceil` and `floor` act on non-negative operands, shares are in permille, and every Attention result is the **discrete, run-quantised integer** of the integrator (the level `L` and baseline `B` in mAU, 1 AU = 1000 mAU = one walking tick of noise, six ticks per run), recomputed from `attention_integrator` with the light and power terms zeroed unless a row says otherwise; the closed-form `ln` and `e^` estimates of the specialist drafts are used only as labelled cross-checks. Three caveats apply to every number. (1) Every sortie time is a **lower bound** while the tool-swap duration is unregistered (`T_EQUIP`, SN OQ-SN-6, carried as 0), and `pickup` and `drop` are TAPs with no registered duration (carried as 0). (2) Every Attention result depends on the [PLACEHOLDER] values of `U_TOOL`, `U_LOUD`, `TAU_ATT_TICKS`, `ATT_THRESHOLD`, `HOLD_PM` [PLACEHOLDER], `B_table`, `TELL_DRAW_LO` [PLACEHOLDER] and `TELL_DRAW_HI` [PLACEHOLDER]. (3) Every route figure rests on **assumed node anchors**: Derelict Authoring publishes room rects, door spans and the `arrive_*` cells but no node anchors, so legs are Manhattan distances from door centres to an anchor tagged `[ASSUMED anchor]`, and Layout's `route_length_px` governs once published (DA-29, ASK-BS-D1). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Four more caveats follow from the rulings. (4) The carry burden `U_BURDEN` 7 [PLACEHOLDER] is Attention's registered value and its recalibration is run (F-26): the D.2 figures that use them quote Attention's integrator with the decay suspended while salvage is held (delegated ruling R5), and D.2 uses Attention's fixed 312-tick golden walk-in where D.1 scales the walk-in with the route *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*. (5) The pod glow's light term is Emitter State's `[PLACEHOLDER]`: the lit figures printed below are snapshots without it, and `REF_GOLDEN` is regenerated with it. (6) The 13-tile `htr_a` leg is the pre-ruling authored anchor; the ruled decision route is 21 to 28 tiles (Derelict Authoring places it) and both are printed. (7) Derivations of this amendment were run with the same integer recursion that reproduces the golden figures (1,756,600 mAU noise-only peak; 3,394,795 mAU lit peak) exactly. *Orchestrator ruling: the specialist drafts disagreed on three inputs; this GDD adopts the checkpoint's `TELL_DRAW_LO` 900 for the played tell (K1), Sanity's run of 12 ticks, 5 per second, for dwell (SN conventions; the primary draft assumed 10 per second), and the registry's per-step leak column of IDB-7 as already-halved (the primary draft applied `OPEN_END_RATE_PM` twice).*

DA's 28-tile one-way carry bound (1344 ticks): (a) 0.116, (b) 0.068, (c) 2775, **0.056**, fails narrowly. **Finding (C-BS-11):** a SCAN passes Sanity's 5 percent test on no MVP route under any reading; for reading (c) the carry alone would have to be at least `3120 - 945 - 486` = 1689 ticks (35 tiles), for reading (a) 3120 ticks (65 tiles, past Suit's vacuum budget `VACUUM_BUDGET_S` 27 s (22 tiles each way walking out and carrying back, 34 carried both ways; AC-SE-75a); A has no unbreathable stretch, so it binds B only) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — confirming review, Suit R6 pod derivation)*. It is not a defect at the MVP, because class (d) ships no junk: Sanity itself says an item that near "is not worth a trip and the check is not the point" (SN D.7). It is a constraint on VS-A junk placement: any junk a SCAN is meant to disprove must sit at least 3120 ticks of `T_home` from the console on the chosen reading, and DA's bounds must not be tuned to satisfy this. The cheap rung is the breath-step (pick up and feel `cue_load`, `C_check` is the pickup), valid only while no stowed class masks the carried one (`held_mass_cue`, `STOWED_CUE_FLOOR_CLASS` [PLACEHOLDER]).

637	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
638	|---|---|---|---|---|
639	| `t_aboard_s` | int s | 0 to about 480 | the session; counted from `pod_settle` to departure, the pod leg is not aboard (SN-5 E1) | time off the home body |

641	| `REC_IDLE` | int mSU per run | 1 | Sanity (registry: `REC_IDLE`) | quiet recovery aboard |
642	| `SAN_MAX`, `STAGE_ENTER[1]` | int mSU | 100,000, 70,000 [PLACEHOLDER] | Sanity (registry: `SAN_MAX`, `STAGE_ENTER`) | the level scale and the stage-1 entry threshold |
643	| `SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR` | int ticks | 12 | Sanity | one drift run |
644	| `t_target_s` | int s | 300 (design target, not registered; 180 to 300 [PROVISIONAL: creative-director], Tuning Knobs) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | BS-20 | the upper bound of the median first-sortie *W_ABOARD* (arrival to the departing console press, D.1); the concept's five-minute loop is the W_LOOP figure, the single target (BS-20), whose design-expectation W_ABOARD share is about 259 s (lint-guaranteed about 229 s) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, so 300 s here is the ceiling checked against stage 1 and not a second target *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |

648	**Output Range:** `dwell_msu` 0 to 45,600 for 8 min (2400 runs at 19); the ordering check is boolean.

650	**Example:** `t_stage1_s = ceil(30000 / 19) / 5` = 1579 / 5 = **315.8 s (5.3 min)**, as Sanity states (SN:344, a playtest hypothesis) `[UNV: Sanity re-runs its D.4 and D.8 under the X11 band change; STAGE_ENTER[1] is not changed by that ruling as read here]` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The orderings: design target 300 s <= stage-1 315.8 s (nests, with 15.8 s of slack) and stage-1 315.8 s < Web Map's safe sortie 480 s < `CELL_S` 1200 s. The fuel floor therefore tolerates a longer sortie than the sanity budget does; that is acceptable (the world shows the sanity cost, not a timer) and is recorded as C-BS-12 for Web Map and Sanity. The autosave loss ceiling (340 s, 5.7 min: SL's `loss_max` 20,400 ticks, D.9) is a different axis *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Second sortie.** The nest above holds for a first sortie from `SAN_MAX`. 655

668	| `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` | int ticks | 1800 | registry | the downed time before death |

Soft: row (a) endogenous Graph tell (EXOGENOUS cut descriptors open none); row (b) Attention tell with fewer than `W_MIN_WARNING_S * TICK_RATE` = 600 ticks left (FAIR mode, provisional); `GATE_SOFT_STATES` CHANNELLING, STAGGERED, IN_POD; row (c) any bound seat's `vitals_state` at CRITICAL or worse (user ruling X7 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*); the death restore also steps back one generation when `T_downed - g_r.T < W_MIN_WARNING_S x TICK_RATE`, and a post-DOWNED refractory of 600 ticks applies | Save/Load SL-5, SL-8 | what defers a due save; `CARRY_WALK` is not a gate state |

673	**Example:** the last generation was written at tick 7600 and the cut completes at 10,000: age 2400 is over the 1800 gap, so the cut is eligible at once; the player is IDLE or `CARRY_WALK`, neither a gate state, so it is written at the next 300-tick poll (window at most 300 ticks, 5 s) and a death on the carry restores to *after the cut*. A cut that completes 600 ticks after a generation waits 1200 ticks (20 s) for the gap; if the player is capping (CHANNELLING) or a tell has under 600 ticks left, it defers further. A save deferred 7200 ticks is written `RISKY`, and a death within `DEATH_LOOP_WINDOW_TICKS` 3600 of restoring a `RISKY` generation steps back one generation (SL-8), so a doomed save cannot trap the player. Without the read, a cut 10 s after a generation waits for the interval generation 10,200 ticks (170 s) later, plus any gate deferral (at most `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 7200 ticks, 120 s; 18,000 ticks, 300 s, in total at the worst). A whole 5-minute sortie therefore fits inside one worst-case loss. *Design-time.*

695	## Edge Cases
696	
697	*Format.* Each case is `If [condition]: [exact outcome]. [rationale]`, ends in its owner's rule-id (Boarding adds no behaviour, BS-1, so an outcome is always an owner's), and carries its id `EC-BS-n` at the end of the bold condition. Cases are grouped by theme; the audit additions of the checkpoint (K15: a DESTROYED node, a store module, a restore in `IN_POD`, the stowed plate, the door that mixes cold) are EC-BS-3, EC-BS-4, EC-BS-40, EC-BS-45 and EC-BS-20, and the dead-bus case (K4) is EC-BS-17. Numbers are design-time and rest on D.1 to D.10. Web Map's constants are registered [PLACEHOLDER] values (see the Format note of Core Rules).
698	
699	### A. Zero, maximum and out of range
700	
701	- **If the player presses `begin_cut` with the welder in hand (`START_EQUIPPED_SLOT` 2) or with no cutter in hand (EC-BS-1)**: the verb answers `NO_TOOL` as an outcome after the press, nothing is cut and no tool-channel tick accrues; `equip_tool` to slot 1 is the fix and its duration is unregistered, so every sortie time stays a lower bound (BS-2 step 1; IA-5, SE-11, SN OQ-SN-6). The wrong tool is an honest, cheap failure, not a hidden gate.
702	- **If the player presses `begin_cap` while carrying, or tries to `equip_tool` the welder with hands full (EC-BS-2)**: both are `BUSY`; the cap is a bare-handed welder act, so the order is cut, cap, then pick up, which follows from "never auto-carried" and not from a rule (BS-8, BS-9; IA-28, SE-11). A second `begin_cap` on an already capped stub is `INVALID_TARGET` (IA-26).
703	- **If the node being cut is DESTROYED (EC-BS-3)**: the cut yields `scrap_count` of its repair part and **no module**; there is nothing to carry, the parts are STOWED stock (they ride the body, not the hands), and the cut's noise is spent regardless. A DESTROYED machine is the loudest thing in its room and was never worth a module (IDB-17, LSG:772; K15).
704	- **If the module being cut is a store (the bus battery `b_a2`, the lamp battery `b_a1`) (EC-BS-4)**: its `stock` is discarded into the Graph's `discarded_*` counters so the conservation invariant still closes, and a reinstalled store starts at stock 0 (IDB-18 (i)). A battery has no fluid port, so it leaves no stub; the island re-solves on the next run and what ran on it goes dark, `b_a1` being the stored energy behind A's one residual lamp (DA-27, `[derived]`), so cutting it ends the visible unknown and is a cost the player caused (IDB-18, K15).
705	- **If a second module is wanted while one is carried (EC-BS-5)**: `pickup` answers `BUSY`; the player drops the first in a safe room and shuttles, or leaves it for a second hop, and a second hop costs a second `HOP_FUEL_ML` [PLACEHOLDER] (D.6). The spare `mod_breaker_junction` and `htr_a` cannot ride in the same hop (IA-28, SE-12).
706	- **If a stowed stack cannot take the pickup (a glowstick shelf of 2 with 3 already stowed, or a second `part_hull_plate`) (EC-BS-6)**: the pickup is rejected with Suit's immediate `STACK_FULL`, nothing is taken and nothing is deleted; the stack stays on the shelf and the player throws or uses one first. `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` [PLACEHOLDER] 4 and the plate's `stack_max` 1 are the structural bound (IA-28, SE-12, IDB-15).
707	- **If the player holds a tool in the HAND holder when a CARRIED-class yield is picked up (EC-BS-7)**: the pickup is admitted, because "needs hands free" means no carried instance and a held tool is a different holder (SE-12). Recorded as an ask to Interaction to confirm the wording (ASK-BS-I5); until then the sortie tests treat it as admitted (IA-28).
708	
709	### B. The carry-admitted set, doors and drops
710	
711	- **If the console row is refused and the player presses the pod console while carrying (EC-BS-8)**: the press is `BUSY` with no prompt; the module must be dropped first and stays aboard exactly as left, persisting on the dormant derelict, and the carry-home branch is lost. **This state is not shippable for the MVP (BS-9):** it removes the carry home, the loop the MVP exists to test, so the producer treats the refusal as a stop and not a degrade. With a BREACH running it would be the abandon cost, but the failure escalates to the producer as a design blocker and is not an accepted state (BS-9 fallback; C-BS-1; IA-5, WM-24).
712	- **If the carried def is not in the focused hardpoint's `compatible_defs` (EC-BS-9)**: there is no prompt at all, an immediate answer that reads only the carried def and the hardpoint's declaration and never a module-body field, so it is not an oracle (BS-18; MSA-26, IA-11).
713	- **If a FAILED-`hp` instance is installed (EC-BS-10)**: it installs as a FAILED module, `condition_bp` carrying through unchanged, and the home island treats it as dead; no verb refused the install and no reason named the condition, and the consequence is visible in the Graph's channel (a dark lantern, a dry trail, no output) (BS-18; IDB-17, IDB-18, LS-22).
714	- **If a CLOSED door lies on the carry route (the home `door_cargo_s`, or a door the player shut behind them) (EC-BS-11)**: the door face shows its ordinary V4 plate and `set_opening` is Applied (not `BUSY`); the carrier presses it, waits `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` 30 [PLACEHOLDER] and walks through with `carry_ref` unchanged; a door shut as a containment tool is the player's own cost on the way out; during a TELL or BREACH the legal alternative is to abandon the module (BS-10, BS-13; IA-5, IA-24, IA-28). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
715	- **If every candidate cell for a `drop` is blocked (a threshold square, nine blocked cells) (EC-BS-12)**: `drop` answers immediate `OBSTRUCTED` and the module stays carried; the player steps back a tile and tries again. Door cells answer `NONE` from `floor_tile_at`, so a drop never lands on one, and A and B corridors are 3 wide, so the risk cells are door thresholds only (BS-10; IA-28, DA-7).

Harm to a crewmate is not a choice a sane player can make: it needs a deliberate lit `begin_harm` channel (IA-31) **and is admitted only while the attacker's sanity is system-verified below the harm threshold** (Sanity's `actor_sanity_below_harm_threshold`, which reads the SIM `harm_eligible` bit; a sane actor's attempt is `NOT_ELIGIBLE` and does nothing; SN-11); **the victim sees the attacker's palette leak and sanity tell before eligibility opens** (`tell_on` leads `harm_eligible` by `SAN_TELL_LEAD_S`, SN-10); **and the incident is attributed to the web** (Interaction's call to Sanity's Class B mutator `record_harm_event(actor, victim, tick)` at harm-channel completion, SN-13), not to the player. Friendly fire is lethal by the user's decision ("death is a bitch"), but only the web's work can open it (Pillar 4(c); anti-pillar: no intentional PvP; BS-24 G-1 and G-8; IA-25, IA-31). Vertical Slice B: at MVP (one seat) no target exists.
784	
785	### K. Degenerate strategies
786	
787	- **If the player strips a wreck node by node (EC-BS-55)**: each module is a carried trip, a hop and a walk, the faucet is the authored node list and salvage-once, the left derelict persists as left, and a hazard room is lethal at eight cuts; there is no safe farm and no refill (BS-16; DA-21, IDB-17, IDB-29, D.4).
788	- **If the player cuts several modules in one visit and carries one per hop (EC-BS-56)**: the noise is Attention's whatever the carry (a chain of cuts trips a tell in the fifth cycle with the beam on, D.2), the yields lie where they fell and the derelict persists; the stockpile on the deck is a cost the web hears and not a store the player owns (BS-7; IA-33, D.2).
789	- **If the player stands still aboard to wait out a threat (EC-BS-57)**: listening is a stance and idle pushes nothing, but dwell is Sanity's price: 19 mSU per run net, stage 1 after 315.8 s; there is no refuge in waiting (BS-4; PC-10, SN E1, D.8).
790	- **If the player tries to cut in the dark to dodge exposure (EC-BS-58)**: a dark cut is impossible, the act gate needs the target lit, and a lit job is a visible job in the exposure ledger (BS-5; IA-6, EM).
791	- **If the player seals doors behind them to contain what follows (EC-BS-59)**: it is a legal Pillar 3 act with a cost on the way out (a closed door met while carrying, EC-BS-11); nothing in Boarding forbids it and no content closes a door for them (BS-10; IA-24).
792	- **If the player waits between the cut and the lift (EC-BS-66)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*: nothing is held, so the decay runs and the level the lift starts from falls (the yield lies on the deck while the player waits in `a_spine`; the printed sweep treats the wait as idle and `REF_GOLDEN` regenerates it with the walk) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; at 28 tiles, lit, FIXTURE-312, waits of 0, 300, 900 and 1800 ticks leave live shares of 140, 120, 93 and 66 permille (any lit wait floors at 26), and an 1800-tick wait in the dark leaves none (the tell opens 480 ticks into the carry with 864 ahead, inside every played draw). This is intended: **patience before the lift is legitimate restraint** (P3), and it is priced by the existing rules and not by the burden: Sanity's aboard dwell (19 mSU per run net, 2,850 mSU for a 30 s wait, D.8), the lethal cold if the player waits beside the yield in `a_machine` (D.4), the lamp cell if lit (D.10), and the time anything else has to arrive. The burden does not cover a yield within reach; the decision it prices is the carry's. K3 is asserted over the lit sweep, and the dark wait is reported and not asserted (D.2 K3; AT-5, F-26).
793	- **If the player drops the module at the tell, outwaits it and re-takes the same module (EC-BS-67)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*: the abort completes 810 ticks after the drop standing still lit (600 at the pre-glow dark floor), and the rearm keys on the item (Attention AT-10): re-taking the same module before `rearm_until_T` ends the rearm on that run, so there is no fresh `TELL_REARM_TICKS` immunity; the burden and the suspended decay resume and the tell re-opens about 156 ticks into the resumed carry (`rem` 870 at 28 tiles, so the second tell fits every played draw), and waiting out the whole rearm first only moves the re-opening to about 228 ticks (`rem` 798). This is intended: the player trades about 13.5 s of stillness, Sanity's dwell and the risk of what comes in that time for a carry that fits, which is restraint priced in time and not the cheap freeze the ruling set out to price (X3). A different item leaves the rearm in place (BS-13; AT-10, F-26).
794	- **If the tell opens with the carrier on a door cell or still inside `a_machine` (EC-BS-68)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: a `drop` never lands on a door cell (Interaction's `drop_placement`) and answers `OBSTRUCTED` when every candidate cell is blocked (EC-BS-12), and standing in an open doorway or inside `a_machine` spends the lethal-cold budget (D.4, EC-BS-20), so the drop-and-outwait answer is worse there than in the open spine. **Computed onset (2026-10-28)** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: measured as distance along the carry route past the CENTRE of `door_a_spine_machine` (DA C.2 (420, 504)); the carry starts at the cut point, in-room leg 204 + d with d = `REF_CARRY_CUT_OFFSET_PX` 24, so 228 px, and `V_CARRY` is 1 px per tick, so tick = px. The tell onset `t_x` = 318, 336, 360, 384 (lit pre-lift dwells 0, 300, 900, 1800) lies 318 - 228 = 90, 108, 132, 156 px past the door centre (1.9 to 3.25 tiles; 66 to 132 px beyond the far face if the door cell is one 48 px tile deep, DA to confirm); the beam-off, home-lamps-off, both-off and dark-1800 variants (`t_x` 348, 432, 468, 480) lie 120, 204, 240, 252 px past it. If the built route's longer 732-tick walk-in lowers `t_x` (the main review estimates `live_pm` about 180/160/120/80, i.e. `t_x` about 282 to 372, [UNV], not an oracle) the lit onset moves to about 54 to 144 px; the envelope across both conventions is 54 to 156 px. So the lit tell opens 1 to 3 tiles north of the doorway, inside the open-door cooled stretch (about 288 of the reference ticks, DA D.18) and next to a door cell on which `drop` answers OBSTRUCTED: this IS EC-BS-68's bad case. Derelict Authoring is asked to put a decision reach there (ASK-BS-D4 (d), OQ-BS-31) (BS-13; IA-28, DA-28).

796	### L. Simultaneous rules
797	
798	- **If the cut completes on the run in which the level crosses `ATT_THRESHOLD` and the tell opens (EC-BS-60)**: both happen, because the cut's effect lands at completion only (IA-25) and the tell is drawn at entry from its own stream (AT-8) and neither owner reads the other; the player meets the tell with the yield on the deck and not in the arms, and the choice of D.3 (carry, or drop-free run) is available at once. The LOUD one-shot is part of the intake that opened the tell, which is the "weigh the noise" cost made visible (BS-7; IA-25, IA-33, AT-8).
799	- **If the player cancels a cut on the same tick the actor is staggered or an abort cause fires (EC-BS-61)**: `cancel_channel` wins and the hook finds no record, so the ledger entry is written once by the cancel and the abort cue is not played (IA-15); the stagger itself keeps the module (BS-9; PC-8, PC-9).
800	- **If a tell's abort condition and its breach-due tick fall on the same run (EC-BS-62)**: the abort wins, one transition, and no breach opens; a player who is below `theta_HOLD` for `ABORT_HOLD_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] at that run is saved by the margin they earned (BS-13; AT-10).

953	### Lane (read first)
954	
955	Boarding & Salvage registers no state, hook, command, mutator, read view or notification (BS-1), so **it produces no visual event of its own**. Every pixel in a sortie is drawn by an owner: the HUD (prompt, bar), the character and tool renderer, Interaction's V8, pickup and drop completions, the Graph and Failure & Trail (the medium at an open end, lamp brightness, room air), Suit (breath, visor fog), Assembly (the seat, the seam), Web Map (pod transit) and the 2D lighting stack (beam, glowstick pool, exposure). This section therefore does three things and only three:

957	1. **Art direction Boarding owns (BS-22):** the open-end pieces and cap pieces (kit gap K-9), the empty-pedestal kerf state, the one shared carried-module sprite and its pose, and the loose-yield sprite rules.
958	2. **Composition constraints** on visuals other owners draw during a sortie: what the sortie must never show (a value, a condition, a loot glow, a ghost, a meter) and what it must keep legible (the way home, the trail that outruns a carrier, the medium at an open end).
959	3. **Classification** of every sortie visual into the truth grammar (below), so Sanity's drift stages and the field-check ladder (BS-14) know what may lie.
960	
961	Where an owner already specifies a visual, this section cites its row label and does not restate it; anything restated would be an ownership absorption and a drift risk. **Vocabulary guard (G-9):** "graft", "severed", "bleed" and "stump" are design prose only; no asset name, slice name, palette note, sprite brief, VFX brief or audio brief uses them (the one exception is the Graph's own descriptor name, which is a data id and never a sprite label). Asset tokens use `end`, `cut`, `cap`. The sprite brief for an open end reads "a cut pipe end", never an organ metaphor (ART 4.4: flesh and violet are reserved for sanity leaks; the ship is a body only in the player's reading, never in the pixels).
