1013	### Animation and motion constraints
1014	
1015	**The carry pose and its lints (AD-BS-1, AD-BS-2).**
1016	
1017	- *Pose.* Both arms raised, the module centred over the helmet, 24 x 14 px at most, bottom edge at least 2 px above the crown; five drawn facings (S, SE, E, NE, N), three mirrored (ART 5.6); the module is symmetric, so a mirror is free.
1018	- *Silhouette (tier 1, ART 5.6).* At 25 percent scale, no colour, no contour, the figure reads helmet circle + pack rectangle + a block breaking the outline *upward*. The module must not merge into the helmet circle (at least 2 px clearance), or it would break the "only perfect circle on a perfect rectangle" rule (ART 3.2).
1019	- *Chest-lamp lint (ART 5.1, ART 8.9 item 18).* In every carry frame at every facing: no module, arm or limb pixel within 3 px of `anchor_chest_<facing>` (the chest point keeps `|x| <= 2`), and the beam axis ray from that anchor is clear of module pixels for its first 12 px. At S, SE and E the module is behind the beam; at NE and N the helmet and pack already occupy the ray and the module sits above the crown (about 20 px or more from the anchor by the ART 5.1 ratios). Measured against the real anchor slices before approval.
1020	- *Height budget.* Figure 55 px + 2 px gap + module at most 14 px = 71 px, under the 72 px wall front face, so the module never pokes into the wall cap layer along a wall.
1021	- *Contour and layering.* The carried sprite has a 1 px Void Steel contour like any hero object on the character layer (ART 5.1; supporting environment never does). It has **no loop hue and no dialect marks**: Graphite mid with Graphite lit plate edges, so every carry looks the same (closes IA Open Question 23 / CE-24). Tool layer above the figure; `anchor_carry_<facing>` supplies the per-frame offset (a new anchor name, ASK-BS-AD2).
1022	
1023	**Locomotion (ART 5.2, stiff-weighted).** Carry is a walk variant of 8 frames, deliberate, no helmet bounce, no squash, no overshoot. Stride length matches `V_CARRY` (1 px per tick = 60 px/s): **zero foot slip at 60 px/s is an import lint** (ground contact measured per frame); the cycle is re-timed, not the walk cycle slowed. The pack's breath rise (2 to 3 px) continues while carrying; the load signature does not change the silhouette or the walk timing (mass never changes `V_CARRY`, IDB-21). Idle while carrying is the raised hold held still with pack breath only. Pickup and drop transitions are 2 to 3 frames each, no flourish, no ease-in-out beyond a held frame. No exaggeration except Controller- and Suit-driven stagger, recoil and collapse frames; **a carry stagger keeps the module** (PC-8): the module wobbles at most 1 px with the body and is never thrown, dropped or tossed by a stagger frame (a forced drop is a downed event only). Facing is locked during channels (five drawn facings).
1024	
1025	**Cuts, not fades (ART 7.3 spirit).** The module-to-pedestal swap, the loose-sprite appearance, the pickup swap, the cap appearance and the open-end medium ending are all **single-frame cuts**; the optional VS settle on the yield is the only eased motion and has no overshoot. Persistent world motion in a derelict during boarding is limited to dust in the beam, the residual lamp (steady), open-end media (FT) and the player's own breath and steps (ART 2.6, "nothing else moves unless the player moves it"; ART 6.4: nothing decorative moves). **Nothing on or around a salvage node idles, bobs, pulses, glints or sparkles to attract the eye** (G-5, ART 6.4 cap). The HUD bar and prompt follow Interaction's motion list unchanged (no settle, tremor or glide on the bar; the glide is reserved for lying readings, ART 7.3). No HUD element flashes above 3 Hz (HR-13); no full-frame flash on cut completion, hop, breach or pickup.
1026	
1027	**Reduced motion (HR-8) and photosensitivity.** Open-end medium propagation and the failure-trail animation are **never suppressed** (they are the truth channel); dust drift may slow; the carry cycle is unchanged; the Alarm sweep becomes a static mark plus sound (ART 7.3). The cutter and welder sparks obey the 3 Hz ceiling by construction (stepped, stochastic, localized at the grip anchor, never full-frame); the Chemlight pool wanes monotonically and never pulses. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Reduce flashing defaults ON at first launch (user ruling X10, D79), and the flash-counting unit (`ceil(n_transitions / 2)`), `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` weighted per area and the creative-director exemptions are Pixel Pipeline's and the HUD's (user ruling X9), cited and not defined here.
1028	
1029	**What a "decide" frame is made of.** Per ART 6.5 ("spend light to read it") the three verdict sentences are distributed across rooms (cause in one, the crew's verb in another, absence in a third); an empty pedestal with a clean kerf is the **absence** sentence for a module the crew themselves cut, and a never-salvaged node is whole. Boarding adds one composition constraint to Derelict Authoring and the generator: **a cut mount must not be mistaken for a dead-ship feature.** The player's kerf (clean and linear, no soot cloud) must be distinguishable from an authored dried-trail scorch (radial arc, ART 3.3) at a glance and in greyscale; the distinction is geometric (line versus radial), not tonal.
1030	
1031	### Truth-channel classification
1032	
1033	Four classes, because the run rulings (R9, R10) and the dead-bus finding (K4) need a finer grid than "consequence versus module-body":
1034	
1035	- **T, consequence channel of record** (the Graph's closed list, LSG:44): compartment temperature, O2 and pressure as the body feels them; frost, mist, scorch and drip trails; hiss, creak and whistle at a descriptor's anchor; lamp brightness (including a node lantern dark or lit); draught. Never lies; lies about it are not permitted. The falsifier of record.
1036	- **A, anchor**: never shifts under hallucination (ART Corollary, HR-6): beam colour, shape and radius; the HUD frame, prompt plate and bar; the character sprites and hand tools; the shared carried-module sprite; filaments at the cone edge (attention is not sanity); glowstick pools; a crewmate's beam.
1037	- **S, supporting, corroborating, not of record**: undisturbed dust and interrupted props (verdict grammar, ART 6.5); the hum of a machine (an Audio class, FT:207; true-state audio in the consequence channel, LSG:976, but not in LSG:44's enumerated list, so true-state corroboration and not the falsifier of record until the Graph rules, C-BS-4); the residual lamp; a dried trail on a module's own fitting where Derelict Authoring placed a dead fault (a candidate field check, never a guarantee, FT:71).
1038	- **M, module-body, corruptible** (PF-5, LS-22): a module's sprite, its gauges and sight-glass faces, an inspect card, a module's own wear state, the loose-yield sprite, a door panel lamp (DA AD-11).
1039	- **Authored structure and props (TRUTH_ST, PF-5 row 15, provisional)**: the pedestal rect and the empty shelf; the Filter may add phantom copies, never edit.

1068	**The falsifier statement carried into the art for the `scr_a` beat (BS-17).** Visually, a FAILED scrubber on a dead bus is indistinguishable from a healthy unpowered one by any T-class pixel. Its falsifiers are SCAN, or waking the bus with the spare breaker and reading the lantern. The only art obligation is that the two lanterns (`scr_a`, `pump_a`) share one sprite and one lit/dark treatment, so a woken bus gives an unambiguous contrast.

1088	*Loop hues and the open-end pieces.* Hue is redundant with shape (ART 4.0 principle 2; 3.3). 1170	## Game Feel
1171	
1172	Boarding & Salvage has no input, no frame and no animation of its own (BS-1), so its feel is the feel of **what the composition makes the owners' systems do in sequence**: how long the player is made to stand still before a take, how soon the world answers a cut, how slow and how loud the way home is, and how legal it is to put the prize down. Every number below is either cited from its owner (never restated as ours) or derived from an owner's value by a Formulas entry here. **Units:** 1 tick = 16.7 ms (`TICK_RATE` 60); a tile is `TILE_PX` 48 px; speeds are `V_WALK` 2, `V_RUN` 3 and `V_CARRY` 1 px per tick (24, 16 and 48 ticks per tile). Every sortie duration is a **lower bound** while the tool-swap time is unregistered (`T_EQUIP`, SN OQ-SN-6). Placeholders carry the owner's tag. The target emotion is **a held breath, then a heavy walk**: slow, deliberate, exposed, with one door out that is always open.
1173	
1174	### Feel reference
1175	
1176	**Borrow:** *Project Zomboid*'s carried burden that changes how you move and its timed contextual actions (a linear bar, cancelled by moving, no skill check); the hands-free chest lamp of *Pandorum* (the beam stays on the job while both hands work and while they are full); *Lethal Company*'s run back with hands full and the real story of dropping the scrap to survive; *Alien: Isolation*'s stillness as a strategy. **Anti-reference:** a numeric weight readout or mass-scaled speed (Zomboid's moodle), a repair minigame or quick-time event (a UI surface that could leak module-body truth and a rhythm demand the "I can leave now" test forbids), a motion tracker (an Attention meter in another form, AT-20), and any treasure framing (a pickup glow, a reward chime, a sting).
1177	
1178	### Input-to-feedback chain (the sortie, in order)
1179	
1180	| # | Player act | What the player sees and hears | Latency or duration | Owner |
1181	|---|---|---|---|---|
1182	| 1 | Press the console (`pod_hop`), hands free or full | keycap drop and press cue at the Applied result; the black window; the avatar and cargo are not drawn | ack in the same render frame, Applied at most 1 tick later; the leg and settle are **945 ticks (15.75 s)** at Web Map's [PLACEHOLDER] figures | Interaction, Web Map |
1183	| 2 | Arrive | the dark room, the beam, one residual lamp, dust; the pod hush ends at the settle | the actor is IDLE at once; the prompt shows after the HUD debounce `PROMPT_SHOW_DEBOUNCE_TICKS` 13 (217 ms, HUD-owned, registered) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* | Web Map, HUD |
1184	| 3 | Stand still (listen) | hiss and creak where lit, Attention's occasional floor-gated hull creaks (AT-26), pack breath, dust in the cone; **nothing else** | idle pushes 0 noise (PC-10); the Attention excess decays on its own constant (`TAU_ATT_TICKS` 1800 [PLACEHOLDER], 30 s) | Controller, Attention |
1185	| 4 | Walk to the node | the beam sweeps; the prompt appears only for a lit, focused node | 24 ticks per tile, 24 AU per tile | Controller |
1186	| 5 | Press and hold `interact` on the node (`begin_cut`) | keycap drop and the first work pose at once; the bar appears at fill 0; sparks at the grip | ack at most 1 frame; Applied at most 1 tick; the first effect of the channel at `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6 ticks; the bar then fills in stepped px | Interaction, HUD |
1187	| 6 | Keep holding (the cut) | a linear bar with a needle-mark, the 6-frame work loop, TOOL-class tool sound; the module stays on its mount | `SALVAGE_CHANNEL_TICKS` 240 [PLACEHOLDER] = **4 s**; the LONG class bar of 40 px interior is 6 ticks per art px | Interaction |
1188	| 7 | The cut completes | in **one frame**: the module becomes an empty pedestal with a linear kerf; the yield sits on the deck; open-end media start; the LOUD one-shot sounds; work loop and sparks stop; the bar holds full for `BAR_HOLD_DONE_TICKS` 12 then cuts | Applied inside the tick the channel completes; `U_LOUD` 180 [PLACEHOLDER] is pushed on that tick; no success sting | Interaction, Attention |
1189	| 8 | Release or move mid-cut (abort) | the fill snaps empty, the break-notch holds 12 ticks, the module is untouched, no half-kerf | the move wins within 1 tick (PC-7); the partial is kept for `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` 600 [PLACEHOLDER] (10 s) | Interaction |
1190	| 9 | Optional: swap to the welder and cap (`begin_cap`) | the stub's hiss and medium stop on the same tick as the cap piece appears | `CAP_CHANNEL_TICKS` 90 per stub = 1.5 s, plus an unregistered swap | Interaction |
1191	| 10 | Tap `interact` to pick the yield up | the loose sprite is replaced by the raised-hold carry sprite **in the same frame**; the prompt becomes `G . Drop`; the breath takes the load signature | depress at the press, click at the Applied result (1 tick); 2 to 3 frames of lift; the breath no later than the pickup frame | Interaction, Suit |
1192	| 11 | Walk home carrying | a third of a run: **48 ticks per tile**, no helmet bounce, no foot slip; the beam stays on; a trail or the dark leans in | `V_CARRY` 1 px per tick (60 px/s, 1.25 tiles/s); 48 AU of locomotion noise per tile whatever the mass (IDB F-13), plus 336 AU of burden per tile while salvage is held aboard the wreck (`U_BURDEN` 7 x 48, Attention F-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)* | Controller, Suit |
1193	| 12 | A tell opens | only the cone rim changes; the audio component starts no later than the visual | a played tell is `TELL_DRAW_LO` 900 [PLACEHOLDER] to `TELL_DRAW_HI` 1800 [PLACEHOLDER] ticks (15 to 30 s); in the shortest, a carry covers at most 18 tiles; under the ruled carry burden it opens 318 ticks (5.3 s) after the pickup, inside the walk (D.2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)* | Attention, Lighting |
1194	| 13 | Press `drop` | the arms lower in 2 to 3 frames, the module sits at the placement cell, the pace jumps to `V_RUN` (16 ticks per tile, 56 tiles in 900 ticks) | free, instant, unlit-legal; the next TAP waits `TAP_REARM_TICKS` 12 | Interaction, Controller |
1195	| 14 | Meet a closed door while carrying | the door's ordinary plate *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | the press costs `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` 30 [PLACEHOLDER] | Interaction |

1198	
1199	So the answer to "I started a cut" is a bar and a work pose within one frame, a module that **does not leave its mount for four seconds**, and then, in one frame, a pedestal, a pile and a bang. The answer to "I lifted it" is a changed breath and a prompt that has lost every verb but one. Nothing in this chain is gated on a Boarding tick, because Boarding has none.
1200	
1201	### Weight (the carry is the felt cost)
1202	
1203	- **The ratio is the feel.** Carry : walk : run is **1 : 2 : 3** in px per tick and **3 : 2 : 1** in ticks per tile (48, 24, 16). A 13-tile frame is crossed in 5.2 s walking and 10.4 s carrying. Noise per tile is **24 AU walking, 48 AU carrying, 64 AU running** (`NOISE_PER_TICK` walk 1, carry 1, run 4 [PLACEHOLDER], D.1 and D.2; locomotion only, and a salvage carry aboard the wreck adds 336 AU of burden per tile, D.2 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*): carrying is the slowest *and* louder-per-tile than walking, and running is the loudest. Because speed never changes with mass, the 6 kg core and the 90 kg cell feel identical in pace; the difference is the breath (SE-28) and nothing else.
1204	- **No ramp, no slide.** Carry starts and stops instantly like the walk (PCI Game Feel); there is no acceleration curve to read as weight. The weight is the *constant* low speed.
1205	- **Hands full is a verb loss.** On pickup every prompt in the world vanishes except `G . Drop` and, at a fitting hardpoint, the console or a door face, its one press (BS-9) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The player feels the carry as a narrowing of what the world offers, not as a number.
1206	- **The pace is the lesson.** A trail, a draught or an alarm sweep that outruns a carrier teaches retreat without text (ART 2.8): at `V_CARRY` the web's propagation is faster than the player; at `V_RUN` after a `drop` it is not.
1207	- **The body tells the truth.** Stagger is an input lock and an animation, never a shove; a carry stagger keeps the module; the walk-only cap at CRITICAL vitals is read off the visor fog and the breath (PCI), never a banner.
1208	
1209	### Snap targets (what is one frame, and what is never eased)
1210	
1211	| Moment | Target | Why |
1212	|---|---|---|
1213	| Module to pedestal-with-kerf | one frame | a cut, not a dissolve (ART 7.3 spirit) |
1214	| Loose sprite to carried sprite | same frame | no fly-to-inventory; no inventory exists |
1215	| Carried sprite to seated machine | one frame | the install is a seat, not a flourish |
1216	| Cap piece appears and the medium ends | same tick | the consequence ends when the act ends (P1) |
1217	| Open-end medium starts | the tick the cut completes | the price is visible at once |
1218	| Work loop and sparks stop | the tick the cut completes | no recoil or overshoot (IA recovery 0) |
1219	| Yield settle | none at MVP; VS optional at most 6 ticks, a 4 px drop, no bounce | no eased motion near a salvage node (G-5) |
1220	| Prompt hide | the same render frame the target is lost or unlit | a prompt for an unlit object would lie |
1221	| Rejection | a cut and a dull cue; no shake, flash or red | rejections never decorate (IA V-10) |
1222	| Full-frame effects on cut, hop, breach, pickup | none | HR-13 and the no-flash rule |
1223	
1224	### The three rhythms of a sortie
1225	
1226	1. **Boarding rhythm (ART 2.6).** Cold, dead, patient. The player is made to stand still before they are allowed to act: the arrival room offers only the beam, dust, a dried trail and the hull's creaks, and every action after it costs light. Target dwell before the first cut: the player chooses; the design target is that **a player who pauses 2 s or more before the first cut is typical**, not forced (X-BS-2). Nothing moves unless the player moves it.
1227	2. **The tell (ART 2.7).** Beam, ambient, radius, temperature and direction do not change; only the rim of the cone gets busier. The tell is **10 to 30 s** by Pillar 2 and in play **15 to 30 s** (`TELL_DRAW_LO` 900 to `TELL_DRAW_HI` 1800 [PLACEHOLDER]); a carry begun at tell entry covers at most 18 tiles (`tell_window_fit`, D.3), so a carry still ahead of more than 18 tiles when the tell opens cannot beat the shortest tell; under the ruled shape the tell opens 318 ticks into a carry of about 21 to 28 tiles, so the *decision* "keep walking with it, or set it down" is live in kind and thin in margin (140 permille of the draw at 28 tiles; the pass line is the boarding spike's, AC-BS-132) (D.2, D.3, **OQ-BS-27**) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. A cut begun at tell entry completes (240 ticks) and leaves 660 ticks, 13 tiles.
1228	3. **The breach (ART 2.8).** Controlled panic. Alarm Red sweeps for 2 to 3 s, a failure trail runs along a graph edge faster than a carrier walks, and the answer the world teaches is *drop it and go*. `drop` is free; the run at `V_RUN` 3 is three times the carry; the console is one press; the hop is always allowed. There is no forced drop and no refusal (BS-13).
1229	
1230	### The emotional arc of the reference sortie (design-time, not a meter)
1231	
1232	Mapped to BS-2's steps and the art bible's rhythms. Times are illustrative targets for the reference sortie (`htr_a` to `hp_cargo_heater`), not lints.
1233	
1234	| Step | Target emotion | Art state | Flow note |
1235	|---|---|---|---|

1434	## Acceptance Criteria
1435	
1436	*Conventions.* GIVEN / WHEN / THEN. Tags: **(auto)** automated and deterministic; **(lint)** a static check; **(review)** read by a human against the text; **(manual)** a playtest with people; **(spike)** a time-boxed technical or design probe; **(UI)** or **(visual)** a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/` (plus lead sign-off for visual); **(advisory)** measured and reported, not asserted. Every row ends in the rule or formula it proves: `[BS-n]`, `[D.n]` or `[Cross-References]`. Rows marked **blocked** wait on a named ask or owner answer and are not waived; rows marked **conditional** apply only if a named ask is refused; rows marked **deferred** wait on a Vertical Slice system and carry that blocker. Rows tagged **BLOCKING** are gates on the implementation of this system: it is not implementation-complete, and the slice does not ship, while any BLOCKING row is red, and no sign-off waives one (AC-BS-25, AC-BS-92 and AC-BS-51b; AC-BS-51a is deleted by the OQ-BS-4 ruling) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Rows described as **a precondition of the MVP playtest** (AC-BS-77, AC-BS-122, AC-BS-123) gate the playtest and not the implementation. Row ids are stable: the numbers are not in file order because the qa-lead's added rows (AC-BS-81 to AC-BS-121) sit with the group they belong to, and AC-BS-122 was added at stage 12; AC-BS-123 to AC-BS-126 were added by the 2026-10-27 design review, AC-BS-127 to AC-BS-131 by the user rulings of the same day, and AC-BS-26, AC-BS-105 and AC-BS-121 were deleted by the review and AC-BS-51a by the ruling and their ids are not reused *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
1437	
1438	*Where the tests live (story type: Integration, with UI and Visual/Feel parts).* Boarding has no code (BS-1), so there is no unit under test: every (auto) row is an **integration test** that drives the owners' real code (Attention's integrator, Interaction's handlers, Suit, Assembly, Save/Load, the Graph) through a headless script plus a Web Map stub, and belongs in `tests/integration/boarding-and-salvage/` (test names `test_boarding_<scenario>_<expected>`). The UI and visual rows need **retained screenshots in `production/qa/evidence/boarding/`**; they are blocking and are not waived at `qa.level: minimal`. **Do not re-implement an owner's formula in a Boarding test:** rows that assert a number from D.1 to D.10 read the value out of the owner's running code under the fixture (Attention's `attention_integrator`, the Graph's leak step, Web Map's `hop_fuel`, Sanity's drift) and compare it with the golden value printed here, so a retune of a placeholder updates the expected number and not the test's logic. Every duration is in ticks at `TICK_RATE` 60; every Attention figure is the run-quantised integer recomputed from `attention_integrator` (mAU) with the owners' [PLACEHOLDER] values (`U_TOOL` 4, `U_LOUD` 180, `TAU_ATT_TICKS` 1800, `ATT_THRESHOLD` 6000, ring-1 `B_table` 300). Route figures use the assumed anchors of D.1 and are regenerated when Layout's `route_length_px` lands (AC-BS-5). The headless fixtures use Web Map's command through a **WM stub** that implements `pod_hop` as a body transfer with the published leg and settle ticks, because the Chart Table and the pod body are not part of Boarding's test. **The reference script runs with fixture dwells of 0 (`REF_ZERO_DWELL`, AC-BS-6, exactly 3612 ticks at the pre-ruling 13-tile anchor, and the `T_sortie_floor` that D.1 computes from the published anchors once Derelict Authoring lengthens the decision route); the noise golden schedule of D.2 (`REF_GOLDEN`) adds a 12-tick pickup dwell and a 30-tick console approach, over the same 60 door ticks (AC-BS-14).** *Observer protocol for every (manual) row:* a response counts when the observer, using a pre-agreed phrase list, records a spoken reference to the named concept within 10 s of the trigger; two observers code independently and a disagreement counts as not met. Manual thresholds are the provisional MVP thresholds `[PROVISIONAL: creative-director]` (creative-director ruling, stage 12: adopted as written) until a second round of eight or more testers promotes them. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
1439	
1440	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Two fixtures, named.** **`REF_ZERO_DWELL`** is the reference script with every dwell and every unregistered TAP or swap duration carried as 0 (AC-BS-6: exactly 3612 ticks at the pre-ruling anchor, recomputed from the published anchors after the ruled route lands). **`REF_GOLDEN`** is the generated golden-schedule file of D.2 (walk-in 312, doors 60 idle, cut 240, pickup dwell 12, carry 624, console approach 30) with its variants and with the `REF_ZERO_DWELL` schedule; it is produced by running the schedules against the owners' running code and is never typed. They share the route and differ only in dwell, so a figure from one is never quoted as the other. **Snapshot rule.** Every figure printed in a row below that rests on a [PLACEHOLDER] is a *snapshot at the defaults*: the test reads its expected value from `REF_GOLDEN` or from the owner's running code and compares it with the live constants, the printed number is documentation, and AC-BS-114's range sweep is what proves no row hard-codes it. The independent **oracle cases** (D.2 O-1 to O-3, D.3's abort arithmetic) are computed by hand and are never read from `REF_GOLDEN`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

findings.finding: Evaluable as written, but circular.
